text.p: Sweden's Svenska Handelsbanken gave a robust indication of the health of the country's banking sector on Monday when it posted first quarter earnings well above expectations.

Operating profit after loan losses rose 14 percent to 1.73 billion crowns ($226.9 million) in the first three months of the year, beating the expected 1.64 billion suggested by a Reuter poll of 10 analysts.
The report sent Handelsbanken shares higher, up five crowns to end at 226 and up three from 223 before the figures hit stock market traders' screens. Handelsbanken is Sweden's largest bank.
Profit was boosted by lower loan losses as well as by higher net interest and commission income, but also by the bank's February acquisition of mortgage lender Stadshypotek for 22.9 billion crowns.
Stadshypotek was included in earnings as of February 26, the bank said, adding that it had not changed the comparison figures from the first quarter of last year to reflect the acquisition.
Analysts were relieved to see that Handelsbanken had decided to keep Stadshypotek bank, which promises an innovative future.
"Stadshypotek bank is a modern, well-managed telephone bank with a good computer system," Jonny Sylven at Swedbank told Reuters.

"By keeping it, Handelsbanken could attain a new way of thinking. There have been some worries that Handelsbanken haven't kept up with the technical development. It has its own telephone bank, but it's not something it pushes."
Sylven also pointed to the positive development of loan losses, which fell 68 percent to 130 million crowns.
"Loan losses have developed favourably, despite the bank taking over Stadshypotek," he said, adding that Handelsbanken had written off some loan losses and put them in the goodwill pool.
By taking over Stadshypotek, the bank built up goodwill of 5.9 billion crowns which it plans to write off over 10 years.
Net interest income also had a positive effect on profits and rose 17 percent to 2.61 billion crowns.
"Almost half of the increase in net interest income stems from increased lending volumes, partly following the acquisition of Stadshypotek," the bank said in a statement.
"Excluding Stadshypotek, margins between deposit and lending rates were largely unchanged."
The other half of the increase, about 200 million crowns, stemmed from trading related activities, the bank said.
Net commission also contributed to the rosy picture and showed an 18 percent increase to 797 million crowns, mainly lifted by increased securities trading profits.
Net financial items declined to a six million crown gain from a 492 million crown gain.
On the negative side, the bank noted that bad debts increased by 51 percent to 4.67 billion crowns or 0.8 percent of lending following the acquisition of Stadshypotek.
The Swedish bank sector has seen large restructuring this year with Handelsbanken taking over Stadshypotek and Swedbank announcing it would merge with Foreningsbanken .
Speculation about a merger between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken took off last autumn, but merger talks broke down earlier this year. Analysts expect the banks to resume talks. ($ = 7.625 Swedish Crowns)
